QF.id: Cat III AIF Overview and Growth_21

answer.text: The fund entity borrowing from market sources for making investments

explanation.text: The Logic: The page 19 footnote of the source defines leveraging at fund level as the fund entity itself borrowing from market sources in order to make investments as part of its investment activity. The Trap: Investor-level borrowing, capital calls and sponsor commitments are separate concepts; pages 35-36 confirm that fund-level leverage is a defining feature of Category III AIFs. Note: The distinction matters because the obligation to repay borrowed money sits on the fund, not on the investor.
